additions.source_quote: חוֹלָם הוּא בְּחִינַת הַמְתָּקָה, כַּמּוּבָא בְּכִּתְבֵי הָאֲרִ"י ז"ל, שֶׁחוֹלָם – גִּימַטְרִיָּא שָׁלֹשׁ הֲוָיוֹת, שֶׁהֵם מַמְתִּיקִין שְׁלֹשָׁה אֱלֹקִים שֶׁבַּגָּרוֹן
additions.notes: Explicit bechina: the cholam vowel IS the aspect of sweetening/hamtaka. The Rebbe grounds this in Arizal's teaching that cholam = gematria of three divine names (YHVH) that sweeten the three Elokim in the throat (mochin d'katnut). This is a shared-nature relationship: cholam and hamtaka are two faces of the same reality.
Gematria equivalence: cholam = three names of YHVH. This is a bechina (shared numerical/essential nature), not cause-and-effect.

additions.source_quote: שָׁלֹשׁ הֲוָיוֹת, שֶׁהֵם מַמְתִּיקִין שְׁלֹשָׁה אֱלֹקִים שֶׁבַּגָּרוֹן
additions.notes: The three YHVH names are the agents of sweetening — they sweeten the three Elokim. While there is a causal dimension (they 'do' the sweetening), the Rebbe presents them as the essential identity of the sweetening process itself, via gematria equivalence with cholam.

additions.source_quote: יְרַפֵּא בְּצֵירֵי, בְּחִינַת (יִרְמְיָהוּ ח׳:כ״ב): הַצֳרִי אֵין בְּגִלְעָד אִם רֹפֵא אֵין שָׁם, הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת רְפוּאוֹת
additions.notes: Explicit bechina: the tzeirei vowel IS the aspect of healing/remedies. The Rebbe links the vowel tzeirei to the concept of tzo'ri (balm/remedy) from Jeremiah 8:22. This is a shared-nature relationship — the vowel and the concept of healing are two expressions of the same reality.

additions.source_quote: יְרַפֵּא בְּצֵירֵי, בְּחִינַת (יִרְמְיָהוּ ח׳:כ״ב): הַצֳרִי אֵין בְּגִלְעָד אִם רֹפֵא אֵין שָׁם
additions.notes: Explicit bechina: tzeirei is linked to the verse about the balm of Gilead (tzo'ri). The linguistic connection (tzeirei/tzo'ri) establishes a shared-nature relationship.

additions.source_quote: וְזֶהוּ וְרַפֹּא יְרַפֵּא (שְׁמוֹת כ"א:י"ט) (עִם שְׁתֵּי הַתֵּבוֹת) מִסְפַּר פִּדְיוֹן נֶפֶשׁ. כִּי עִקָּר הָרְפוּאָה – עַל־יְדֵי פִּדְיוֹן דַּוְקָא
additions.notes: Gematria equivalence: the two words 'v'rapo y'rapei' = numerical value of 'pidyon nefesh'. This is a bechina (shared numerical essence), establishing that the Torah's verse about healing is inherently the same reality as redemption of the soul.

additions.source_quote: שְׁלֹשָׁה אֱלֹקִים שֶׁבַּגָּרוֹן, שֶׁהֵם מֹחִין דְּקַטְנוּת, שֶׁיּוֹרְדִין בַּגָּרוֹן
additions.notes: The three Elokim names in the throat ARE the aspect of mochin d'katnut (constricted consciousness). This is a Kabbalistic bechina — two terms for the same spiritual reality. These represent the din (judgment) that needs to be sweetened. Polarity is evil/negative as they represent the state of constriction and judgment.

analysis_notes.summary: Torah #3 of LM2 is a short, focused teaching. The dataset captured only eitza (cause-and-effect) relationships — the core argument that pidyon (redemption) sweetens judgment and thereby enables the doctor to heal. However, the final two lines of the Torah (lines 9-10) contain rich bechina language from the Arizal's Kabbalistic framework: the vowel cholam is an aspect of sweetening (hamtaka), the vowel tzeirei is an aspect of healing (refuot), and the gematria of 'v'rapo y'rapei' equals 'pidyon nefesh'. These bechina relationships were not entered into the dataset and represent a significant gap. The 9 nodes currently in the dataset all participate only in eitza edges and therefore cannot form packages under the bechina-only rule. They should remain unpackaged until the missing bechina edges are added.
